text:
Tess: Quick sync — we need a concrete approach for continuation semantics across Python/TS/Go SDKs. The old page-token + offset stuff is leaking into product and causing weird resume bugs when retries happen. Thoughts on a single forward-compatible "bookmark" format + transport fallback (streaming -> poll)?
Sam: Agree. Bookmark that is opaque to SDKs makes sense. Make it versioned so we can change shape later.
Anya: Versioned opaque token + server-side validation. If token invalid -> 410 with a suggested fallback (e.g., reset to head or re-request start params). Keep token small (<= 512 bytes).
Mike: Go ergonomics: prefer a small struct with ParseBookmark/SerializeBookmark helpers. Avoid exposing raw JSON blobs in public API. Python/TS can be more dynamic.
Tess: Sketch of token: ```b64(JSON) -> {"v":1,"s":"items","u":"<shard-id>","o":12345,"i":"<idempotency>"}``` where o=offset-ish, i=client-provided idempotency token. Servers should ignore unknown fields.
Sam: Nice. For retries: SDK should attach `x-resume-id` header when retrying requests that resumed from bookmark. Server can use it to dedupe if it supported at-least-once semantics. If server can't dedupe, SDK should fall back to re-requesting last N items and de-duping client-side when possible.
Anya: Transport fallback: primary: streaming (chunked gRPC/HTTP2). If streaming disconnects and resume token is present, try a stateless `GET /items?bookmark=...` to fetch a batch, then re-open stream. That path needs explicit backoff and a max-sanity window to avoid duplicates.
Mike: Backpressure concern: streaming clients can be overwhelmed if server bursts. SDK should expose a bounded queue or async iterator with configurable prefetch (default 2 * pageSize). In Go sync iterator return items and block when queue full.
Tess: Edge case: old servers that only support page tokens (no bookmarks). Plan: SDK will translate bookmark->pageToken server-side via a mapping endpoint if available, else fall back to page-based loop with warnings. Deprecation window needed.
Sam: API ergonomics: expose two methods: `listItems(params)` (stateless page API) and `streamItems(params, {resumeBookmark?})` (streams with resume). Keep `resumeBookmark` optional. Document semantics clearly.
Anya: For security, bookmarks must be HMAC-signed (server-side) so clients can't fabricate cursors. Use versioned key ids in token so rotation is possible.
Mike: Telemetry: emit resume success/fail metrics and number of duplicate items trimmed client-side. Console can use to decide default heuristics.
Tess: I'm +1 on bookmark + signed token + streaming-first + GET fallback. Next: create a short RFC with examples per-language, migration plan, and handler sketches for servers.
devex-bot: Created ticket INF-1428 for "Continuation bookmarks + streaming fallback RFC" -> https://tracker.internal/INF-1428 :white_check_mark:
Tess: Action items: @Sam write API surface PR (TS + Python), @Mike add Go helpers + iterator patterns, @Anya draft server-side token format + HMAC rotation notes. Aim to sync next Wed.
Sam: Will start a PR draft today.
Anya: Drafting server notes now, will ping for review.
Mike: I'll stub Go helpers and an example iterator by EOD tomorrow.
Tess: Thanks all. Keeping scope minimal for now: v1 bookmark = resume offset + idempotency + key id. We'll iterate.
